stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, comparing French and English colonization patterns.
stimulus.text: France and England colonized North America in different ways. France sent few settlers — mostly single men who traded furs, married into Native families, and built alliances with the Wendat against the Iroquois. England sent whole families who farmed the land, pushed Native peoples off it, and built towns of their own. Both empires depended on Native peoples at first, but France needed them as partners and England needed their land.
